headings: International Master Franchise and Other Agreements
Internal Dough Manufacturing and Supply Chain System
paragraphs: Domino's is the largest pizza company in the world with more than 22,100 locations in over 90 markets around the world as of December 28, 2025, and operates two distinct service models within its stores, with a significant business in both delivery and carryout. We are a highly recognized global brand, and we focus on value while serving neighborhoods locally through our large worldwide network of franchise owners and U.S. Company-owned stores through both the delivery and carryout service models. We have been selling quality, affordable food to our customers since 1960. We became "Domino's Pizza" in 1965 and opened our first franchised store in 1967. Over the past 65 years, we have built Domino's into one of the most widely-recognized consumer brands in the world. We believe our commitment to value, convenience, quality and new products continues to keep consumers engaged with the brand.

We are primarily a franchisor, with approximately 99% of Domino's global stores owned and operated by our independent franchisees as of December 28, 2025. Franchising enables an individual to be a business owner and maintain control over all employment-related matters and pricing decisions, while also benefiting from the strength of the Domino's global brand and operating system with limited capital investment by us.

Domino's business model is straightforward: Domino's stores handcraft and serve quality food at a competitive price, with easy ordering access and efficient service, enhanced by our technological innovations. Our hand-tossed dough is made fresh and distributed to stores around the world by us and our franchisees.

Domino's generates revenues and earnings by charging royalties and fees to our franchisees. Royalties are ongoing percent-of-sales fees for use of the Domino's® brand marks. We also generate revenues and earnings by selling food and other products to franchisees through our supply chain operations primarily in the U.S. and Canada and by operating a number of Company-owned stores in the U.S. Franchisees profit by selling pizza and other complementary items to their local customers. In our international markets, we generally grant geographical rights to the Domino's Pizza® brand to master franchisees. These master franchisees are charged with developing their geographical area, and they may profit by sub-franchising and selling food, and to a lesser extent, other products to those sub-franchisees, as well as by running pizza stores. We believe that everyone in the system can benefit from the franchise model, including the end consumer, who can purchase Domino's menu items for themselves and their family conveniently and economically.

Domino's business model can yield strong returns for our franchise owners and our Company-owned stores. It can also yield significant cash flows to us, through consistent franchise royalty and supply chain revenue streams, all within an asset-light model. We have historically returned cash to shareholders through dividend payments and share repurchases. Domino's financial results are driven largely by retail sales at our franchised and Company-owned stores. Changes in retail sales are primarily driven by same store sales growth and net store growth. We actively monitor both of these metrics, as they directly impact our revenues and profits, and we strive to consistently increase both metrics. Retail sales drive royalty payments from franchisees, as well as Company-owned store and supply chain revenues.

At Domino's, we believe we have a proven business model for success that has historically driven strong returns for our shareholders. Our Hungry for MORE strategy aims to generate MORE sales, MORE stores and MORE profits. The strategic imperatives of our Hungry for MORE strategy are as follows:

Most Delicious Food: We believe we have the best pizza in the industry, and our menu has even more mouthwatering options beyond pizza. We will continue to showcase the breadth of our menu, while highlighting the deliciousness of our food through our innovative marketing promotions.
Operational Excellence: We are relentless in our focus on convenience, consistency and efficiency for our customers.
Renowned Value: We are committed to continuing to offer competitive pricing and personalized value for our customers that is innovative and memorable.
Enhanced by Best-in-Class Franchisees: Our franchisees play a vital role in driving results and excitement across the more than 90 markets in which we operate.

The QSR pizza category is large, fragmented and highly competitive. In the U.S., we compete primarily against national chains Pizza Hut®, Papa John's® and Little Caesars Pizza® as well as regional, independent and local establishments. We generally compete on the basis of product quality, location, image, service, technology, convenience and price. Our business and those of our competitors can be affected by changes in consumer tastes, economic conditions, demographic trends, geopolitical and reputational considerations, marketing, advertising, pricing and consumers' disposable income. We also compete with other restaurants, as well as order and delivery aggregation companies, which have continued to grow in size and scale in recent years. We have multinational agreements with Uber Technologies, Inc. and DoorDash, Inc. to allow customers to order Domino's products through their respective marketplaces. We compete not only for customers, but also for management and hourly employees, including store team members, drivers and qualified franchisees, as well as suitable real estate sites.

From 2024 through 2025, the U.S. QSR pizza category grew from $42.8 billion to $43.4 billion and is primarily comprised of dine-in, delivery and carryout, with delivery and carryout comprising the two largest segments. Carryout includes both carryout and drive-through occasions. In the U.S., we compete in the delivery and carryout segments of the QSR pizza category. The four industry leaders, including Domino's, account for approximately 61% of U.S. pizza delivery and approximately 51% of U.S. pizza carryout, with regional, independent and local establishments comprising the remainder of the category. Within the U.S. QSR pizza category, we are recognized as number one, with approximately 23.3% total market share based on consumer spending data for the year ending December 2025 (up from approximately 22.5% for the year ended December 2024). We are the market share leader in both delivery and carryout, with approximately 32.9% and 19.6% share in each segment, respectively, based on consumer spending data (Source: Circana, CREST®, twelve months ended December 2025. Data of share information provided by Circana is preliminary and is based on simulated results; data is not considered final until published by Circana.)

Internationally, the QSR pizza category is also fragmented and highly competitive. Outside the U.S., we compete primarily with Pizza Hut and Papa John's which have significant global presence, as well as country-specific national, regional and local pizzerias. We believe that demand for pizza delivery and pizza carryout is large and growing globally, driven by international consumers' increasing emphasis on convenience, and is supported by our proven success of more than 40 years of conducting business abroad.

Our business is not dependent upon a single retail customer or small group of customers, including franchisees. No customer accounted for more than 10% of our total consolidated revenues in 2025, 2024 or 2023. As of December 28, 2025, our largest franchisee based on store count, Domino's Pizza Enterprises (DMP: ASX), operated 3,524 stores in 12 international markets, which accounted for approximately 24% of our international store count and 16% of our global store count. Revenues from this master franchisee accounted for 1.4% of our consolidated revenues in 2025. Our international franchise segment only requires a modest amount of general and administrative expenses to support its markets and does not have a cost of sales component. Therefore, the vast majority of these royalty revenues result in profits to us.

headings: The quick service restaurant ("QSR") pizza category and the food service and food delivery markets in general are highly competitive and such competition could adversely affect our operating results.

If we fail to successfully implement our growth strategy, which includes opening new stores and generating more sales, our ability to increase our revenues and operating profits could be adversely affected.
Increases in food, labor and other costs, labor shortages or negative economic conditions could adversely affect our profitability and operating results.
Shortages, interruptions or disruptions in the supply or delivery of fresh food products and store equipment could adversely affect our operating results.

The food service market is affected by consumer preferences and perceptions. Changes in these preferences and perceptions may reduce the demand for our products, which would reduce sales and harm our business.
Reports of product contamination, food-borne illness or food tampering or other events which may impact our reputation may reduce sales and harm our business.
We do not have long-term contracts with certain of our suppliers, or have contracts which are set to expire, and as a result they could seek to significantly increase prices or fail to deliver.
Any prolonged disruption in the operations of any of our dough manufacturing and supply chain centers could harm our business.

Our international operations subject us to additional risk. Such risks and costs may differ in each country in which we and our franchisees do business and may cause our profitability to decline due to increased costs.

Our earnings and business growth strategies depend on the success of our franchisees, and we may be harmed by actions taken by our franchisees, or employees of our franchisees, which are outside of our control.
Our success depends in part upon effective advertising, and lower advertising funds may reduce our ability to adequately market the Domino's Pizza brand.
Loss of key employees or our inability to attract and retain new qualified employees could hurt our business and inhibit our ability to operate and grow successfully.
We may not be able to adequately protect our intellectual property, which could harm the value of our brand and branded products and adversely affect our business.
We are subject to a variety of additional risks associated with our franchise system and franchisees.
Our current insurance coverage may not be adequate, insurance premiums for such coverage may increase and we may not be able to obtain insurance at acceptable rates, or at all.
Environmental, social and governance matters may impact our business and reputation.
Our substantial indebtedness could adversely affect our business and limit our ability to plan for or respond to changes in our business.
Downgrades in our credit ratings could impact our ability to access capital and materially and adversely affect our business, financial condition and results of operations.
We may be unable to generate sufficient cash flow to satisfy our significant debt service obligations, which would adversely affect our financial condition and results of operations.
paragraphs: For a business as large and globally diverse as Domino's, a wide range of factors could materially affect future developments and performance. In addition to the factors affecting specific business operations identified in connection with the description of these operations and the financial results of these operations elsewhere in this report and our other filings with the SEC, we believe the most significant risk factors affecting our business include the following:

In the U.S., we compete primarily against national chains Pizza Hut®, Papa John's® and Little Caesars Pizza® as well as regional, independent and local establishments. Internationally, we compete primarily with Pizza Hut®, Papa John's® and country-specific national, regional and independent or local companies. We have and may continue to experience increased competition from existing or new companies in the delivery and carryout pizza categories, in addition to competition from order and delivery aggregators and other players both in the pizza category and more broadly, that may create further pressures to grow our business in order to maintain our market share. Competition for both customers and drivers from these order and delivery aggregators and other food delivery services has substantially increased as order and delivery aggregators have grown in size and scale and have diversified the food offerings available for delivery. Additionally, we face competition from supermarkets and meal kit and food delivery providers, with the proliferation of prepared food and meal kit offerings, expansion in meal delivery platforms and services and the trend towards convergence in grocery, deli, retail and restaurant services.

We also compete more broadly with QSRs and other international, national, regional and independent or local restaurants. headings: 國際總特許經營商及其他協議
強大且已驗證的商業模式
內部麵糰製造與供應鏈系統
paragraphs: Domino's 是全球最大的披薩公司，截至 2025 年 12 月 28 日，擁有超過 22,100 個據點，遍及全球 90 個市場，並在其商店內運作兩種不同的服務模式，其中在送餐與外帶業務方面均有顯著的營收。我們是一個高度被認可的全球品牌，並透過我們龐大的全球加盟者網路與美國本公司所有商店，透過送餐與外帶服務模式，專注於提供價值，同時服務當地社區。我們自 1960 年來持續向客戶提供高品質且價格合理的食物。我們在 1965 年成為 "Domino's Pizza"，並於 1967 年開設了第一家加盟商店。過去 65 年來，我們已將 Domino's 建立為全球最受認可的消費者品牌之一。我們相信，我們對價值、便利性、品質與新產品的承諾，持續維繫消費者對品牌的關注。
我們主要為一家加盟公司，截至 2025 年 12 月 28 日，Domino's 全球商店約有 99% 是由我們的獨立加盟者所擁有並營運。加盟模式讓個人成為企業所有者，並可掌控所有與僱用相關的事項與價格決定，同時也能透過 Domino's 全球品牌與運營系統的強大，以較少的資金投入獲益。
Domino's 的商業模式非常明確：Domino's 商店手工製作並提供高品質的食物，以具競爭力的價格銷售，搭配簡易的訂購方式與高效的服務，並透過我們的科技創新加以提升。我們的手工拋擲麵團由我們與加盟者製作並分發至全球各地的商店。

Domino's 透過向加盟者收取特許經營權費用與服務費來產生收入與獲利。特許經營權費用為持續性的銷售百分比費用，用以使用 Domino's® 品牌標誌。我們也透過向加盟者銷售食物及其他產品，透過我們的供應鏈運營（主要在美國與加拿大），以及透過運營美國的多家本公司所有商店來產生收入與獲利。加盟者透過向當地客戶銷售披薩及其他補充商品來獲利。在國際市場，我們通常授予 Domino's Pizza® 品牌的地理權給總加盟者。這些總加盟者負有發展其地理區域的責任，他們可能透過次加盟與銷售食物，以及在較小程度上銷售其他產品給這些次加盟者來獲利，同時也透過經營披薩商店來獲利。我們相信，系統中的每個人都能從加盟模式中受益，包括最終消費者，他們可以方便且經濟地為自己與家人購買 Domino's 菜單項目。

Domino's 的商業模式可為我們的加盟者與本公司所有商店帶來強勁的回報。同時，也能為我們帶來顯著的現金流，透過持續的加盟特許經營權費用與供應鏈收入流，皆在一個輕資產模式下進行。我們歷來透過股息發放與股票回購來回饋現金給股東。Domino's 的財務表現主要由我們加盟商店與本公司所有商店的零售銷售所驅動。零售銷售的變化主要由同店銷售成長與淨商店成長所驅動。我們積極監測這兩個指標，因為它們直接影響我們的收入與獲利，我們致力於持續提高這兩個指標。零售銷售驅動加盟者的特許經營權費用支付，以及本公司所有商店與供應鏈收入。
在 Domino's，我們相信我們擁有經過驗證的商業模式，歷來為股東帶來強勁的回報。我們的 Hungry for MORE 策略旨在產生 MORE 売出、MORE 商店與 MORE 利潤。我們 Hungry for MORE 策略的戰略重點如下：
最美味的食物：我們相信我們擁有業界最好的披薩，而我們的菜單還提供了超越披薩的更多令人垂涎的選擇。我們將持續展示我們菜單的廣度，同時透過我們的創新行銷活動，強調我們食物的美味。
運營卓越：我們對顧客的便利性、一致性與效率保持極度專注。
Renowned Value: 我們致力於持續提供具競爭力的價格與個性化的價值給客戶，並具創新性與難忘性。
Enhanced by Best-in-Class Franchisees: 我們的加盟夥伴在推動結果與熱情方面扮演關鍵角色，遍及我們經營的超過 90 個市場。

The QSR pizza category 是一個規模龐大、分散且高度競爭的產業。在美國，我們主要與 Pizza Hut®、Papa John's® 和 Little Caesars Pizza® 等全國連鎖品牌競爭，以及區域性、獨立與地方性 establishments。我們通常以產品品質、位置、形象、服務、技術、便利性與價格作為競爭基礎。我們的業務與競爭對手的業務可能受到消費者口味變化、總體經濟狀況、人口趨勢、地緣政治與聲譽考量、行銷、廣告、價格與消費者可支配所得的影響。我們也與其他餐廳以及訂購與外送聚合平台競爭，這些平台在近年來持續成長。我們與 Uber Technologies, Inc. 和 DoorDash, Inc. 籤訂國際合作協議，讓消費者能透過他們的市場平台訂購 Domino's 產品。我們不僅競爭客戶，也競爭管理與 hourly 員工，包括商店團隊成員、駕駛與合格的加盟夥伴，以及合適的實體店面。

從 2024 年至 2025 年，美國 QSR 比薩產業的規模從 428 億美元成長至 434 億美元，主要由堂食、外送與自取組成，其中外送與自取為兩大分部。自取包括自取與 drive-through 的情形。在美國，我們在 QSR 比薩產業的外送與自取分部進行競爭。四大產業領導者，包括 Domino's，在美國外送市場佔有約 61% 的市場份額，在美國自取市場佔有約 51% 的市場份額，其餘由區域性、獨立與地方性 establishments 組成。在美國 QSR 比薩產業中，我們被認可為第一名，根據截至 2025 年 12 月的消費者支出資料，我們的總市場佔有率約為 23.3%（較截至 2024 年 12 月的約 22.5% 增加）。我們在外送與自取兩大分部均為市場佔有率領先者，根據消費者支出資料，我們在外送分部的市場佔有率約為 32.9%，在自取分部的市場佔有率約為 19.6%（來源：Circana, CREST®，截至 2025 年 12 月十二個月的資料。Circana 提供的市場佔有率資料為初步資料，基於模擬結果；資料在 Circana 公佈前不視為最終資料。）
國際上，QSR 比薩產業同樣分散且高度競爭。在美國以外的地區，我們主要與具有全球規模的 Pizza Hut 和 Papa John's 競爭，以及國家性、區域性與地方性的比薩店。我們認為，全球對比薩外送與自取的需求龐大且持續成長，這是由國際消費者對便利性日益重視所驅動，並受到我們在國際市場經營超過 40 年的成功經驗所支持。

我們的業務並未依賴單一零售客戶或小型客戶羣，包括加盟夥伴。在 2025 年、2024 年或 2023 年，沒有客戶佔我們總合併營收的 10% 以上。截至 2025 年 12 月 28 日，根據商店數量，我們最大的加盟夥伴 Domino's Pizza Enterprises (DMP: ASX) 在 12 個國際市場經營 3,524 家商店，佔我們國際商店數量的大約 24% 以及全球商店數量的大約 16%。來自此總加盟夥伴的營收在 2025 年佔我們合併營收的大約 1.4%。我們的國際加盟分部僅需少量的總務及行政費用來支持其市場，且不包含銷售成本組成。因此，這些 royalty 營收的絕大多數會轉化為我們的利潤。

headings: 快速服務餐飲（"QSR"）披薩類別以及整體餐飲服務與餐飲外送市場競爭激烈，此等競爭可能對我們的營運成果產生不利影響。
若我們未能成功執行成長策略，包括開設新店及增加銷售額，我們增加收入與營運獲利的能力可能受到不利影響。
食品、人力及其他成本的增加、人力短缺或負面經濟條件可能對我們的獲利能力與營運成果產生不利影響。
鮮食產品與門市設備供應或配送的短缺、中斷或中斷可能對我們的營運成果產生不利影響。
餐飲服務市場受消費者偏好與觀感影響。這些偏好與觀感的變化可能減少對我們產品的需求，進而降低銷售額並損害我們的業務。
有關產品污染、食源性疾病或食品竄改或其他可能影響我們聲譽的事件可能降低銷售額並損害我們的業務。
我們與部分供應商並無長期契約，或契約即將到期，因此他們可能大幅提高價格或無法履行交付義務。
任何持續的經營中斷，可能影響本公司零組件製造及供應鏈中心的運作，進而損害本公司業務。
本公司國際業務使我們面臨額外風險。這些風險與成本可能因國家而異，且可能因成本增加而導致本公司利潤率下降。
本公司獲利與業務成長策略依賴於我們特許經營商的成功，我們可能因特許經營商或其員工所採取的行為而受損，而這些行為超出我們的控制範圍。
本公司成功在一定程度上取決於有效的廣告，廣告經費減少可能降低本公司有效行銷 Domino's Pizza 品牌的能力。
失去關鍵員工或無法吸引並留住新進合格員工，可能損害本公司業務，並抑制本公司運作與成長的能力。
本公司可能無法充分保護智慧財產權，這可能損害本公司品牌與品牌產品的價值，並對本公司業務產生不利影響。
本公司因特許經營系統與特許經營商而面臨多種額外風險。
本公司現有保險 coverage 可能不足，保險 premium 可能增加，且本公司可能無法以可接受的價格或甚至無法取得保險。
環境、社會及治理議題可能影響本公司的業務與聲譽。
與本公司負債相關之風險
本公司龐大之負債可能不利於本公司業務，並限制本公司規劃或應對業務變動之能力。
本公司信用評級遭降級可能影響本公司取得資金之能力，並對本公司業務、財務狀況及營運成果產生重大且不利之影響。
本公司可能無法產生足夠之現金流量以償付重大之債務償還義務，此將對本公司財務狀況及營運成果產生不利影響。
paragraphs: 對於一家如 Domino's 這樣規模龐大且 globally diverse 的企業，許多因素都可能對未來的發展與表現產生重大影響。除了影響特定業務運作的相關因素，這些因素已於本報告中與這些業務運作及這些業務運作的財務結果之描述部分以及我們其他提交至 SEC 的文件中說明外，我們認為影響我們業務的最重要風險因素包括以下內容：

在美國，我們主要與 Pizza Hut®、Papa John's® 和 Little Caesars Pizza® 等全國性連鎖店競爭，同時也與區域性、獨立及地方性設施競爭。國際上，我們主要與 Pizza Hut®、Papa John's® 以及特定國家、區域性及獨立或地方性公司競爭。我們可能持續面臨來自現有或新興公司在外送與自取披薩類別中的競爭，此外，來自訂單與外送聚合平台及其他參與者（不僅在披薩類別，也更廣泛地）的競爭，也可能造成進一步壓力，以促使我們成長業務以維持市場佔有率。來自這些訂單與外送聚合平台及其他餐飲外送服務的客戶與司機競爭，已因這些訂單與外送聚合平台的規模與規模擴張，以及所提供的外送餐點種類更加多元而顯著增加。此外，我們也面臨來自超級市場與餐點組合及餐飲外送服務的競爭，因預備餐點與餐點組合服務的普及、餐點外送平台與服務的擴張，以及零售、餐飲與超市服務趨向整合的趨勢而產生影響。
我們也更廣泛地與 QSRs（速食餐廳）及其他國際性、全國性、區域性及獨立或地方性餐廳競爭。整體餐飲服務市場、餐飲外送市場以及 QSR 市場，在食品品質、價格、服務、形象、便利性與概念方面競爭激烈，且常受到以下因素的影響：
• 消費者口味與觀感；• 國際性、全國性、區域性或地方性經濟條件；
• 廣告行銷、宣傳與價格策略，包括價格上漲與折扣，以及宣傳活動；
• 總體經濟變動、可支配所得購買力與人口結構趨勢；
